guide.dimensionalflux.cover.title: Dimensional Flux Guide
guide.dimensionalflux.cover.subtitle: Energy without cables, across worlds
guide.dimensionalflux.cover.intro: Cables are lovely until the hundredth one. This book shows how to send Forge Energy through the void between dimensions, keep every network under control and charge your gear on the way. Read in any order; the ribbon always brings you back.

guide.dimensionalflux.start.welcome: Dimensional Flux moves energy §bwithout cables§r. A Dimensional Emitter takes energy from a generator or battery, a Dimensional Receiver hands it to a machine, and both can sit in different corners of the world, or in different dimensions. Between them lies a §bnetwork§r: a name, a color and a list of who may use it.
guide.dimensionalflux.start.energy: Everything here moves §eForge Energy (FE)§r made by other mods. Dimensional Flux generates nothing on its own: it only carries, stores and hands out what your generators produce.
guide.dimensionalflux.start.path:
§b1.§r Mine the Dimensional Flux Shard deep underground.
§b2.§r Turn shards into a Dimensional Core and Dimensional Blocks.
§b3.§r Craft a Dimensional Emitter for your generator and a Dimensional Receiver for your machine.
§b4.§r Create a network on either of them and link the other.
§b5.§r Later: a Dimensional Battery to store, a Dimensional Controller to watch and charge items, a Tesla Broadcaster for whole rooms and a Dimensional Configurator to copy settings.
guide.dimensionalflux.start.screens: Right click a device to open it. The middle shows its network, name, priority, rate and what it moved last. The tabs on the sides open the other windows: choosing a network, statistics, members, network options, a new network, and the gear for the screen look.
guide.dimensionalflux.start.windows: Each window can be dragged by its top bar and several can stay open together. Escape closes the device screen and every window. Buttons that step through values go forward with a left click and back with a right click.
guide.dimensionalflux.start.guide: Turn the pages with the arrows, the ←→ keys or the mouse wheel; the cyan ribbon at the top goes back to the contents. Underlined names show the item when you hover them. Lost the book? You get one the first time you pick up a shard, and a new one is made like this:
guide.dimensionalflux.materials.ore: The Dimensional Flux Shard grows in small veins of 2 to 8 blocks, about as rare as diamonds. Look in stone from Y 16 down to −16 and in deepslate from Y 0 to the bottom, most often between −58 and −50.
guide.dimensionalflux.materials.mining: The ore rests dark and lights up with purple and blue sparks when touched, used or walked on. An §eiron pickaxe§r or better drops one shard; Fortune adds more, Silk Touch keeps the ore block.
guide.dimensionalflux.materials.core: The heart of every device. Copper, Obsidian, two Eyes of Ender and one shard make four cores.
guide.dimensionalflux.materials.block: Shards and Dimensional Cores packed into one solid block: the frame of the bigger devices, and a fine purple floor for the brave.
guide.dimensionalflux.materials.miner: With Dimensional Flux Miner installed, you can use its Miner to produce Dimensional Flux Ore continuously in the Overworld. Process the ore to obtain Dimensional Flux Shards.
guide.dimensionalflux.networks.what: A network joins every device linked to it, wherever it is. Energy that enters through one device can leave through any other in the same tick, across dimensions. A device belongs to one network at a time.
guide.dimensionalflux.networks.create: Open a Dimensional Emitter or a Dimensional Receiver, click the + tab, give the network a name and a color and press Create. Then open the other devices, open Choose Network on the left and click the network: done.
guide.dimensionalflux.networks.security: §bPublic§r: anyone can link a device. §bPrivate§r: only members. §bLocked§r: guests need the password. In Choose Network an open lock marks public networks and a closed one the others.
guide.dimensionalflux.networks.color: The color tints the devices, their particles, the screens and the map. Pick one of the sixteen dye colors or press Customize for any color you like.
guide.dimensionalflux.networks.members: The Members tab lists the players. The owner can make someone a User or an Administrator, or block them; a block wins over every other kind of access and unlinks that player's devices.
guide.dimensionalflux.networks.teams: A network can be shared with your scoreboard team (/team) and, with FTB Teams installed, with your party. Everyone on the team gets User access while they stay on it.
guide.dimensionalflux.networks.distribut: In Network Options, §bPriority§r serves each receiver in turn with all it asks for. §bShare§r splits what is left between receivers of the same priority in proportion to what they ask for, so nobody starves when energy is short.
guide.dimensionalflux.networks.delete: Deleting a network unlinks every device on it. Energy stored in a Dimensional Battery stays in the battery.
guide.dimensionalflux.emitter.about: Takes energy from the block it is mounted on and sends it into its network.
guide.dimensionalflux.emitter.mounting: Place it against a generator, battery or any block that gives Forge Energy. It uses only the face it touches. On a floor or ceiling its front follows the direction you were looking.
guide.dimensionalflux.emitter.pull: Generators that push energy fill it on their own; passive stores such as a cell are emptied by the Emitter when the network needs it. Energy is never kept in the Emitter: what nobody uses goes to a Dimensional Battery.
guide.dimensionalflux.emitter.generators: Several Emitters on the same network add up: one per generator is the usual setup.
guide.dimensionalflux.receiver.about: Hands network energy to the machine it is mounted on.
guide.dimensionalflux.receiver.mounting: Place it against the machine. It delivers only through the face it touches, so machines that accept energy on one side only work too.
guide.dimensionalflux.receiver.delivery: Each tick it asks the machine how much it can take and the network sends just that. For many machines in one room, a Tesla Broadcaster saves a Receiver per machine.
guide.dimensionalflux.receiver.antenna: The antenna moves only while energy flows: a still antenna means the machine is full or the network is empty.
guide.dimensionalflux.transfer.priority: The higher number is served first. A receiver at 5 gets energy before one at 2; at the same priority, order follows the Distribution setting. Negative numbers put a device behind the default 0.
guide.dimensionalflux.transfer.limit: Max Rate caps what a device moves per tick. §bIgnore Limit§r removes the cap altogether.
guide.dimensionalflux.transfer.batteries: A Dimensional Battery is always served after every machine and drawn from after every generator, whatever its priority: it keeps what is left over and fills the gaps.
guide.dimensionalflux.transfer.buffers: Emitters and Receivers hold a small buffer for the next ticks. Any amount passes through while it is being used, but the buffers of a network never keep more than 1,000,000 FE between ticks: the rest goes to batteries, and what no battery can take is lost.
guide.dimensionalflux.transfer.redstone: The torch tab at the bottom left of Emitters, Receivers and the Tesla Broadcaster chooses when they work: always, only with a redstone signal, or only without one. A stopped device stays linked and moves nothing.
guide.dimensionalflux.transfer.chunk: Load Chunk keeps the device's chunk loaded, so a generator far away keeps feeding the network while nobody is near it. Server admins can turn this option off.
guide.dimensionalflux.transfer.backup: A Dimensional Receiver or a Tesla Broadcaster can name a backup network: in Choose Network, right click the network (right click again to clear it). After five seconds without energy on its own network the device moves to the backup, and returns once its own network has had energy for five seconds.
guide.dimensionalflux.transfer.backup_wh: A network has energy when a battery holds charge or an Emitter has energy to give. Home shows "on backup" while a device runs on its backup.
guide.dimensionalflux.battery.about: Stores the energy the network does not use right now and gives it back when it runs short.
guide.dimensionalflux.battery.order: It needs no Dimensional Emitter or Dimensional Receiver: link it to a network and it takes the surplus and covers the shortages on its own, always after the machines.
guide.dimensionalflux.battery.gauge: Eight bars on the block show the stored charge.
guide.dimensionalflux.battery.keep: A broken battery keeps its charge, network and settings in the item. Crafting the battery alone clears its network and settings and keeps the charge.
guide.dimensionalflux.battery.creative: For creative testing: endless energy on every face, also for Emitters.
guide.dimensionalflux.controller.about: The control room of a network: it sees every connection and charges players' items.
guide.dimensionalflux.controller.totals: Its Statistics and Connections show the whole network, not one device: input and output now, over a minute and an hour, the devices, the storage and the top machines.
guide.dimensionalflux.controller.chargin: The Charge Items tab chooses which slots get energy: hot bar, armor, hands and, with Curios, accessories. Apply with groups selected turns charging on for every player who may use the network, in any dimension. A Tesla Broadcaster can do the same inside its area.
guide.dimensionalflux.controller.slots: A total limit in FE/t keeps charging from emptying the network; the infinity button removes it.
guide.dimensionalflux.controller.alerts: In the gear window of a Controller, Deficit alerts warns the network's players in chat when it consumes more than it makes for 30 seconds and its reserve will not last two minutes.
guide.dimensionalflux.tesla.about: Delivers energy to machines inside its configured area without a separate Receiver on every machine.
guide.dimensionalflux.tesla.area: The area tab sets a cube from 9 to 32 blocks and moves it east or west, up or down, south or north, as long as the broadcaster stays inside it. Show Area draws the cube in the world.
guide.dimensionalflux.tesla.preview: Below the sliders, a 3D view shows the area and the machines it will power. Drag with the left button to turn it, with the right to move it, use the wheel to zoom and double click to reset.
guide.dimensionalflux.tesla.machines: This tab lists every machine inside that takes energy. Uncheck one to leave it out, rename it, light it up in the world or give it its own priority and rate.
guide.dimensionalflux.tesla.split: Machines are served in priority order and receive what they accept within their own limits and the Tesla's total limit. In Machines in area, enable §bShare equally§r to divide energy equally within each priority. This switch is off by default. Full machines leave their shares to machines that still need energy.
guide.dimensionalflux.tesla.charging: Its own Charge Items tab charges the players standing in its area, with its own slot groups and limit.
guide.dimensionalflux.tesla.corner: Push the area so the broadcaster sits in a corner of the room and the cube covers all of it.
guide.dimensionalflux.configurator.about: Copies the settings and network of one device to others, and shows what a device is doing.
guide.dimensionalflux.configurator.copy: Sneak and use it on a device to copy; use it on another to paste the network, name, priority and rate. Sneak and use it in the air to clear it. Perfect for a wall of Dimensional Emitter or Dimensional Receiver blocks.
guide.dimensionalflux.configurator.hud: While you hold it and look at a device within 12 blocks, a panel in the corner shows its network, input and output now, over a minute and an hour, and the batteries' charge.
guide.dimensionalflux.configurator.hidde: Hide Block in the gear window makes a device invisible. Holding the Configurator shows a thin outline around hidden devices nearby, in their network color.
guide.dimensionalflux.monitoring.statist: On most devices the chart shows that device alone over 30 seconds. On a Dimensional Controller or a Dimensional Configurator it shows the whole network: input in green, output in red, a balance strip and the storage gauge.
guide.dimensionalflux.monitoring.ranking: Top generation and Top consumption list the ten machines that give and take the most, now or over 10, 20 or 60 minutes.
guide.dimensionalflux.monitoring.connect: The Controller's Connections tab lists the machines of the network. The pencil on a row edits its name, priority, rate and chunk loading.
guide.dimensionalflux.monitoring.highlig: The highlight button lights a machine up for 15 seconds with an outline you can see through walls.
guide.dimensionalflux.monitoring.setting: The gear tab chooses the screen look and particles. Particles and Apply to all devices start enabled. Turn Apply to all off to customize each device; new devices start light with particles enabled. Turn it back on to copy the current device's choices to all devices. These choices stay on your computer.
guide.dimensionalflux.trouble.nothing: Check that both devices are on the same network (the top of the screen), that the Emitter touches the face that gives energy, that the Receiver touches a face that accepts it, and that no redstone tab is stopping them.
guide.dimensionalflux.trouble.slow: Look at Max Rate on both ends, and at priorities: higher numbers are served first. Statistics show whether the network makes enough.
guide.dimensionalflux.trouble.lost: Buffers never keep more than 1,000,000 FE between ticks. Surplus without a Dimensional Battery to take it is lost: add a battery.
guide.dimensionalflux.trouble.unloaded: Devices in unloaded chunks do nothing. Turn on Load Chunk on the device or keep the area loaded.
guide.dimensionalflux.trouble.denied: Private networks only accept members, locked ones ask for the password, and a blocked player cannot use the network at all. Ask the owner in Members.
guide.dimensionalflux.emitter.reactors: A reactor from Bigger Reactors Rework can supply this network. Attach an Emitter to its energy output and use Receivers or a Tesla Broadcaster to power your machines.
guide.dimensionalflux.mod_link: Open the mod page on CurseForge
guide.dimensionalflux.battery.comparator: A comparator on any side reads the stored charge from 0 (empty) to 15 (full). Use this signal to switch backup generators on as the charge falls or stop generation when storage fills.
